subject: stochastic mapping using output from LaGrange

messages.author: d3c9ac62d374695a
messages.subject: stochastic mapping using output from LaGrange
parts:
Hey Nick,

I have a tree that is massive (>9000 tips, with 11 ranges) that will predictably not fit in BioGeoBEARS. However, I think it will run in the C++ version of LaGrange.

My hope is that I could use the maximum likelihood parameter estimates for the DEC model from LaGrange and then pass those to BioGeoBEARS to build stochastic maps from this model fit.

I think it would be straightforward to edit the res$outputs to incorporate the estimates from LaGrange, but studying the stochastic mapping scripts for a stratified analysis, it looks like stochastic mapping also requires the res$condlikes_table, res$relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_[...]_DOWNPASS_TABLE, res$ML_marginal_prob[...]_bottom_below_node, and res$ML_marginal_prob[...]_top_AT_node.

My question then, is whether it would be theoretically possible to get these tables somehow if I know the maximum likelihood parameter estimates from the DEC model already.

Thanks again for your help,

Jonathan

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] stochastic mapping using output from LaGrange
parts:
Hi- on my phone at the moment, but briefly, in general it would be easy, but if you are having a memory error or whatever, then that would occur just the same for calculating the likelihood and ancestral state probabilities once for one set of user -specified parameters, as for doing a full ML analysis. 

Basically, imagine storing in memory a table that has 2*ntips-1 rows and numstates colums , that might be 18,000*2000 for your case. Or the issue could be with parallelization, where it stores P matrices for all 18000 branches. Turning off parallelization would be the solution in thats case. There might be a way to up the memory alotment for R, if you know the error message we could explore more.

The easiest solution would likely be do compromise a little on the max number of areas and reduce the state space.
Cheers, nick
